findings.pdf_says: Page 155 opens with its own paragraph "Format 3 (reference-modification):" and the next paragraph is "identifier-1  reference-modifier-1". On page 154 the Format 2 body is the paragraph "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1" and nothing follows it on that page.
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 6678: "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):" — the Format 3 label is welded onto the end of the Format 2 body line, before the anchor; the page-155 slice then begins directly with "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1".
findings.why_it_matters: 8.4.3.1.2 is a run of label/body pairs (Format 1 … Format 11). With the label absorbed into the previous body, Format 2's body reads "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1 Format 3 (reference-modification):" and Format 3 appears to have no label at all, so any reader or extractor pairing format labels with their general-format bodies mis-attributes both formats.
findings.suggested_repair: Split line 6678: leave "qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1" as the Format 2 body on page 154, and place "Format 3 (reference-modification):" as its own paragraph immediately after the / "## Page 155" scaffolding and above "identifier-1 reference-modifier-1".

findings.pdf_says: 8.4.3.4.4 General rule 1 lists the applicable INVOKE forms one per line. Page 163 prints: "INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier" then "INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier"; page 164 continues with "INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier" then "INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier", followed by a separate paragraph "where:" and then items a) b) c).
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 7078 (end of the page-163 slice): "INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier where:" — three of the four printed forms plus the "where:" lead-in run together on a single line.
findings.why_it_matters: General rule 1 defines the semantics of an inline method invocation by equivalence to one of four distinct INVOKE statement forms. Merged onto one line they read as a single unparsable statement, so the boundaries between the four alternatives (and hence which forms exist) are no longer recoverable, and the "where:" lead-in that governs items a)-c) on page 164 is buried inside that line, orphaning those definitions.
findings.suggested_repair: Restore four separate lines for the four INVOKE forms (keeping the first two before the page-164 anchor and the last two after it, matching the print), and make "where:" its own paragraph immediately before items a) b) c).

findings.pdf_says: Headings printed on page 157 in the normal clause hierarchy: "8.4.3.1.4  General rules" (a fourth-level clause under 8.4.3.1), then "8.4.3.2  Function-identifier", "8.4.3.2.1  General", "8.4.3.2.2  General format", "8.4.3.2.3  Syntax rules".
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 6794-6828: "## **8.4.3.1.4 General rules**", "## **8.4.3.2 Function-identifier**", "### **8.4.3.2.1 General**", "### **8.4.3.2.2 General format**", "### **8.4.3.2.3 Syntax rules**" — heading text wrapped in bold markup, and none of the five carries the anchor that every neighbouring page in this run uses (e.g. page 161: "" + "#### 8.4.3.3.1 General").
findings.why_it_matters: Page 157 is the only page in this batch whose clause headings deviate from the document's own convention: the four-part clause 8.4.3.1.4 sits at markdown level 2, the same level as its uncle 8.4.3.2 (page 161 correctly puts 8.4.3.3.1 at level 4 under 8.4.3.3 at level 3), so a generated TOC shows 8.4.3.1.4 as a peer of 8.4.3.2; and the five missing section anchors mean citations of the form #section-8-4-3-2-2 (the Function-identifier general format, a figure this compiler cites) have no target.
findings.suggested_repair: Renumber the levels to match the convention (#### for 8.4.3.1.4, ### for 8.4.3.2, #### for 8.4.3.2.1/.2/.3), drop the ** wrappers from the heading text, and add the , , , , anchors.
